analysis.title: Up and Adam (Investment Strategy daily, Tuesday, November 17, 2026)
key_insights: Consumer Staples hit a record high ahead of Target and Walmart earnings this week and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 12% YTD, its second widest outperformance since 2008. Raymond James remains underweight and says the rally may be stretched.
Staples faces volatile input costs. Consensus 2027 EPS growth for the sector is +6% versus +16% for the S&P 500. The sector trades at its largest NTM P/E premium to the S&P 500 since at least 2000.

AAA expects 81.5M Americans to travel for Thanksgiving, down 0.1% after three record years. Road and air travel are slipping because of record seasonal gasoline prices and a 17% YoY rise in average domestic airfares to about $800. Travel remaining near record highs suggests consumers still prioritize leisure spending.

October retail sales are expected to rise 0.4% headline, versus a 0.8% gain in September, with control group sales also expected up 0.4%. October CPI rose 0.4% MoM, so expected sales growth would be flat in inflation-adjusted terms.

The Empire State Manufacturing Index fell to 7.8 in November from a nearly five-year high of 25.5 in October but stayed in expansion. New orders and shipments moderated but stayed positive, and employment rose at its fastest pace since June 2022. The prices paid gauge fell to its second-lowest level since the US-Iran conflict began.

AAA's national average retail diesel price fell below $6.00/gallon for the first time since early September. Diesel is still 59% above year-ago levels versus a 24% rise for gasoline. Returning to sub-$4.00 diesel would likely require an end to refinery disruptions in the Persian Gulf and Russia, which could take considerable time. Raymond James remains overweight Industrials and cites trucking and freight rail as beneficiaries of the relief.
Philly and Kansas City manufacturing surveys on Thursday will give further read on manufacturing momentum.

sector_views.rationale: Record high and 12% YTD outperformance versus the S&P 500, with consensus 2027 EPS growth of +6% versus +16% for the market, input cost volatility, and the largest NTM P/E premium since at least 2000.
Falling diesel prices give some relief to trucking firms and freight railroads.

Persistent refinery disruptions in the Persian Gulf and Russia keeping diesel elevated.
